preamble: Regressive nasalization of a front mid vowel before a tautosyllabic or lost nasal consonant is the first step in building a nasal-vowel system. In Portuguese, loss of intervocalic and final n left phonemic [ẽ] (venit > vem [ˈvẽj̃]). Old French nasalized e before nasals (dentem > early Old French [dẽnt]) before lowering it to [ã]. Slavic created the front nasal *ę from *e + nasal before a consonant (Proto-Balto-Slavic *pénki > Proto-Slavic *pętь 'five'), and Polish keeps it as ę.

examples.note: The nasal consonant was lost and left its nasality on the vowel. Brazilian Portuguese keeps [ẽ], while Lisbon later centralized it to [ɐ̃].
e nasalized before the nasal consonant. The resulting [ẽ] then lowered to [ã] in the 11th to early 12th century (modern dent, vent [dɑ̃], [vɑ̃]).

examples.to: Proto-Slavic *pętь > Polish pięć, Old Church Slavonic пѧть 'five'
examples.note: *e + nasal before a consonant coalesced into the front nasal vowel *ę, which Polish preserves as ę (before a stop it is realized as a vowel plus a homorganic nasal, pięć [pʲɛɲt͡ɕ]).
